title: General Probabilities of Causation with Causal Knowledge
abstract: arXiv:2608.12657v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Probabilities of causation (PoCs) characterize individual causal responses that cannot be directly observed and therefore generally require partial identification. Tian and Pearl first derived theoretically sharp bounds for binary PoCs, including the probability of necessity (PN), the probability of sufficiency (PS), and the probability of necessity and sufficiency (PNS). Mueller et al. subsequently tightened the bounds for binary PNS by incorporating causal information encoded in covariates and mediators. More recently, Li and Pearl, as well as Shu et al., extended PoCs to multivalued settings and derived corresponding theoretical bounds. These developments naturally raise the question of whether additional causal knowledge can further tighten the bounds in multivalued settings. translated_title: 具有因果知识的因果概率一般化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12657v1 公告类型：新 摘要：因果概率（PoCs）表征无法直接观察到的个体因果反应，因此通常需要部分识别。Tian和Pearl首先推导了二元PoCs的理论紧致界，包括必要性概率（PN）、充分性概率（PS）以及必要且充分性概率（PNS）。Mueller等人随后通过纳入协变量和中介变量中编码的因果信息，收紧了对二元PNS的界。最近，Li和Pearl以及Shu等人将PoCs扩展到多值设置，并推导了相应的理论界。这些发展自然引发了疑问：额外的因果知识能否进一步收紧多值设置中的界。本文通过纳入协变量和中介变量中编码的因果信息，推导出多值PoCs的更紧致界，从而解决了这一问题。
tldr: 本文通过利用协变量和中介变量中的因果信息，扩展并收紧了多值因果概率的界，实现了更精确的部分识别。
en_tdlr: This paper tightens bounds for multivalued probabilities of causation by leveraging causal information from covariates and mediators, enabling more precise partial identification.
